source_row.rationale: Progressive dyspnea with dull percussion and decreased or absent breath sounds over an area of the chest are classic findings of a pleural effusion (fluid accumulation in the pleural space), warranting further evaluation, such as chest X-ray or ultrasound, to confirm and guide management, potentially including thoracentesis.
source_row.source_detail: Pleural effusion may produce dyspnea, decreased breath sounds/fremitus and percussion dullness; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client reports progressive dyspnea and dull, decreased breath sounds on one side of the chest, and a colleague assumes this is probably just an unrelated abdominal issue causing referred discomfort. The nurse should instead suspect:
